samples.summary: CLI contract statements still claim the file spawns nothing / touches no outside world, but `--coderabbit-latency` reaches `gh` via `execFileSync`
samples.evidence: USAGE at scripts/agent/eval/cost-latency.mjs:1012 says "Writes nothing and spawns nothing." and the module header at scripts/agent/eval/cost-latency.mjs:50 still reads "NOTHING IS WRITTEN AND NOTHING IS SPENT. It reads a store, computes, prints." — neither mentions a subprocess. The new flag path calls `corpusRecords` (cost-latency.mjs:1088) → `fetchCodeRabbitPr` (adapters/coderabbit.mjs:1142) → `gh` (scripts/agent/gh-checks.mjs:26-28), which is `execFileSync("gh", …)`, i.e. a spawned process. The diff dropped "costs nothing" from the usage but left "spawns nothing" and the header untouched, so two statements of the module's own contract now describe the pre-#799 behaviour. Fix belongs on the new code (the USAGE string and the header banner).

samples.summary: `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped to 2 with a breaking reshape of `coderabbit.latency`, but the one downstream consumer of the filed payload never reads `schema_version`
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/eval/report.mjs:597-616 (`costLatencyFigures`) is the only consumer of a filed `cost-latency-v1` score. It accepts any object, emits `payload_keys: Object.keys(payload).sort()` and never inspects `payload.schema_version`; `validateScore` (scripts/agent/eval/store.mjs:383-404) only checks `scorer_id`/`scope`. So the version bump this diff makes is inert downstream: a store still holding a schema-1 payload (where `coderabbit.latency.wall_ms` was a scalar) renders identically to a schema-2 one, and nothing warns. Low practical impact today because nothing files the score yet (the CLI writes nothing), but the counter this diff bumps has no reader to protect.
searchedFor: grep cost-latency / cost_latency across repo and docs

samples.summary: The scorer gains a static import of the network-touching adapter, which its sibling scorer's purity test explicitly forbids for itself
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/eval/cost-latency.mjs:83 statically imports `./adapters/coderabbit.mjs`, which transitively pulls `../../harvest.mjs` and `../../gh-checks.mjs` (adapters/coderabbit.mjs:44-47) into every consumer of the scorer library. The sibling scorer asserts the opposite invariant on itself — scripts/agent/eval/reliability.test.mjs:784-794 checks `reliability.mjs`'s static imports contain no filesystem/network module and that network reads are dynamic imports inside `main()`. `cost-latency.mjs` already uses that dynamic pattern for the store (`await import("./store.mjs")`, line 1043) but not for the adapter, so the stated "library stays pure" property now holds only at call time, not at load time. `complementarity.mjs:59` does the same thing, so this is a divergence between two conventions rather than a break — flagging so the intended one is chosen deliberately.
